# DecompressionFailureConsumed

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 5.3" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Check decompression before consuming data.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$s=gzdecode($bytes); strlen($s);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Check decompression before consuming data.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- D1. Report results of gzdecode, gzuncompress, gzinflate or inflate_add reaching strlen/strtoupper without a dominating strict false guard. Follow direct expressions and unchanged locals. Exclude matching encoder/decoder roundtrips with default encoding and omitted or valid literal compression level.
- D1a. Error suppression does not change the result: a decompression call wrapped in `@` (directly or through the assigned local) is followed like the bare call.
- D1b. A strict false guard is a `=== false` / `!== false` comparison, with the constant on either side, whose other operand is the tracked local or the parenthesised plain assignment that stored the reaching result. It dominates the consumer when the consumer sits in: the `if`/`elseif` branch, `while` body or `for` body (last condition expression) selected by a passing test; a later `elseif`/`else` arm after a failure test; the matching ternary arm (the else arm of a short ternary after a failure test); the right operand of `&&`/`and` after a passing test or of `||`/`or` after a failure test; or the statements following an `if` without alternatives whose failure branch always terminates. Inside a condition, `!` inverts the test, a true conjunction establishes each of its operands and a false disjunction refutes each of its operands. The tested value must be the one that reaches the consumer: reassignment between test and use, or a repeated call, is a different value.
- D2. Resolve builtin functions, extension classes, method receivers, constants and named arguments. Follow unchanged locals and aliases only within the same bounded lexical scope. Require a reachable path; merge branch facts only when all incoming paths establish them.
- D3. Emit one finding at the violating operation, not one per evidence statement. Rebinding, writes, by-reference escape, unresolved calls that can mutate relevant state, and exhausted analysis budgets remove proof.

## Exceptions (no report)

A nested encoder proves matching bytes only when its encoding argument is omitted; argument count does not establish that omission.

- E1. Exclude shadowed builtins, unresolved receivers, incomplete syntax and unknown prerequisite facts. An extension function name alone does not prove an application function is that builtin.
- E2. A dominating valid guard or repair described in Detection prevents the finding. Both legacy noinspection and custos-ignore forms suppress this ID.
- E3. `assert`, `match (true)` arms and a statement-level `$s === false and exit;` are not guards under D1b; such code is still reported unless flow analysis independently excludes false.
- E4. A value the shared flow analysis proves is not false at the use is never reported, whatever form the proof takes: a truthiness or `empty()` test, a loose comparison with `false` or `null`, a type predicate, or an early exit whose `if` also has an `else` branch that continues. So `$s ? strlen($s) : 0` and `$s != false && strlen($s) > 3` are not reported, while the wrong arm or operand of such a test still is. The same holds for a statement that leaves on the failing outcome (`$v !== false or exit;`, `$v or throw …;`, `$v ?: throw …;`), for a failing branch that ends in a call that never returns (a callee declared `never`, or a function or a final or private method every path of which throws or exits), for a test stored in a boolean and tested later while neither the boolean nor the tested variable has been written, and, on PHP 8.0 and later outside any `try` with a `catch`, for a builtin call that returned after receiving the value for a parameter that only accepts arrays, objects or callables: such a call throws a `TypeError` for `false`. A `switch (true)` case is read like the condition of an `if`/`elseif` chain; in a `switch` on the variable itself with constant labels, the cases after a `false` or `null` label and the `default` hold a value that is neither, as does a `true` case. Positions PHP may skip prove nothing: the right side of `??=`, the arguments of a null-safe call and anything chained after `?->`. A null-safe call to a never-returning method does not end the path, and `f(...)` creates a closure without calling `f`. An arm of `match (true)` is read like a `switch (true)` case; an arm that throws, exits or calls a function that never returns takes no part in what holds after the `match`. `|` and `&` between two tests are read like `||` and `&&` for the outcome that fixes both operands (a false `|`, a true `&`), and a strict `in_array($v, [...], true)` over literals that include neither `false` nor `null` excludes both where it holds. `goto` jumps are followed, except in a scope that also contains a `try`, which the flow analysis leaves alone. Where a `goto` label is written before the use, and after the place where its scope first names the checked variable, a variable that can hold the same value, or code that may write any variable (`extract`, `compact`, a variable variable, `eval`, an included file), a jump can land between a guard and the use: only what the flow analysis establishes counts there, and a guard recognised by where it is written proves nothing. Two variables can hold the same value when one is written from the other by a plain assignment, an assignment by reference or `??=`, when a `foreach` takes one out of the other, or through a chain of those; in the value assigned, the receiver and the arguments of a call, the operands of an operator other than `??`, the variables a string embeds and an element key do not count, and a statement that only reads (`echo $prefix . $parts['host'];`) ties nothing. A parameter is named from the start of the function, and a checked expression that reads `$this` or no variable counts every label before it. In a scope the flow analysis does not follow (one that also contains a `try`, a generator, a scope that evaluates or includes code) a guarded use after such a label is therefore reported. A label written before all of that, such as a `retry:` label ahead of the `try` that produces and checks the value, changes nothing, whatever else the function reads beside the checked value; at file level every label written before the use counts. What was established of a `static` local holds until the next call, or code that runs without a call being written (an object converted to text, a magic property or offset access, the destructor of an object a variable held when it is given another value), that may enter the function again and assign the variable. A call of PHP's own counts as such when it may run code of the project: it is given a callback other than the name of a PHP function that only computes on text and numbers (`strlen`, `trim`, `intval` and the like), an object it may convert, or a class name it loads (`method_exists($name, 'm')`, `is_callable('A::b')`, `defined('A::B')`, `new ReflectionClass($name)`), a class to construct (`$statement->fetchObject('Row')`), or it runs what was registered earlier (an error, session or output-buffer handler, the callbacks of a cURL transfer or an XML parser, an iterator wrapped in another). This limits every guard form of this specification, not only the ones the flow analysis reads.

## Fix

No automatic fix. The required repair depends on error handling, data selection, lifecycle ordering or application policy.

All edits use exact byte ranges and preserve comments and evaluation order. Offer no fix when its stated prerequisites cannot be proven or the replacement is unsupported by the configured PHP version.

## PHP versions

Requires PHP 5.3 or later and the referenced extension API. Respect method-specific introduction versions within PHP 5.3–8.5; unsupported optional APIs cannot establish facts. Named arguments require PHP 8.0 or later.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DecompressionFailureConsumed": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DecompressionFailureConsumed
```
